newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae up on view stalemate near end.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae up on view stalemate near end.

text.p: Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) was up 6-7/8 to 133-1/4 Thursday afternoon in a continuation of the move from the prior session, which came in response to news that chief executive Lawrence Hough plans to resign.

"I think that it is investor enthusiasm about the possibility that coalition government may continue at the company and that the stalemate that has existed for the last several weeks can be broken," said Thomas O'Donnell, analyst at Smith Barney.

Neither the Sallie Mae management headed by Hough, nor an opposing shareholder group called the Committee to Restore Value (CRV), was able to gain the support of a majority of shareholders last month when competing privatization plans were put to a vote.
Shareholders have been asked to vote again at a meeting expected to take place in July.
Sallie Mae rose 6-1/8 Wednesday in the initial response to the news of Hough's plan to resign. Hough said he hoped the move would break the deadlock between the two groups.
